strategy_title: Align BLOCK_N tile to actual N dimension to cut bank conflicts
strategy_description: When a GEMM tile dimension (e.g., BLOCK_N) is set larger than the actual matrix dimension (e.g., N=4 but BLOCK_N=16), threads access shared memory with large strides that cause severe bank conflicts (11.8-way) on 74% of shared load wavefronts. Reducing BLOCK_N to match the actual N dimension eliminates wasted masked-out computation, aligns shared memory access patterns to the data layout, and dramatically cuts register pressure (96→39 registers/thread), improving theoretical occupancy (31.25%→37.5%) and reducing L1/TEX throughput from 95.67% to 75.32%. The total instruction count dropped by ~63% (12.8M→4.7M), confirming that the oversized tile was causing massive redundant work.
slow_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_N=16 but actual N=4 — 75% of N-tile is masked/wasted
BLOCK_M = 128
BLOCK_N = 16  # 4x larger than actual N=4
BLOCK_K = 32
# B matrix loaded with stride causing 11.8-way bank conflicts
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K):
    a = load_A_tile(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K)
    b = load_B_tile(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N)  # strided access, bank conflicts
    acc += dot(a, b)
fast_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_N=4 matches actual N=4 — no wasted compute, aligned access
BLOCK_M = 128
BLOCK_N = 4   # matches actual N exactly
BLOCK_K = 64
# B matrix loaded with aligned stride, bank conflicts reduced
for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K):
    a = load_A_tile(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K)
    b = load_B_tile(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N)  # aligned access
    acc += dot(a, b)
applicable_when: SharedMemoryConflicts NCU rule fires with >5-way bank conflicts; BLOCK_N (or BLOCK_M) tile dimension is set significantly larger than the actual matrix dimension; L1/TEX Cache Throughput >80%; high register pressure (>64 registers/thread) limiting occupancy; executed instruction count is suspiciously high relative to problem size
do_not_apply_when: Tile dimensions already match or are smaller than actual matrix dimensions; bank conflicts are low (<2-way); the matrix dimension is large enough that any reasonable tile size is smaller than it; reducing tile size would cause too many kernel launches or insufficient parallelism
framework_notes: In Triton, constexpr tile sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) are set at compile time. When using @triton.autotune, the key insight is to constrain BLOCK_N configs to be <= actual N so that tl.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N) produces valid grid dimensions and masking handles boundary correctly. The same principle applies in CUDA: choosing threadblock tile dimensions larger than the actual matrix dimension wastes shared memory bandwidth and causes strided bank-conflicting access patterns.

strategy_title: Increase num_warps to hide MIO/shared-memory latency
strategy_description: When the CPIStall rule identifies high MIO stall cycles per warp (23 cycles, 56.5% of total stall time) from shared memory operations, and the scheduler shows >85% no-eligible cycles with very few active warps per scheduler (~5.5), increasing num_warps at the Triton launch site can provide more in-flight warps to hide the latency. However, in this case the improvement was marginal (52.51us→51.17us, ~2.6% wall-clock reduction despite 1.55x reported speedup), because the dominant bottleneck remained the 10-way shared memory bank conflicts (80% of shared load wavefronts) which num_warps alone cannot fix — more warps in flight still stall on the same conflicted banks. The strategy is most effective when MIO stalls are caused by latency rather than contention; when bank conflicts are the root cause, fixing the access pattern is necessary first.
slow_pseudocode:
# Launch with default num_warps=4, no pipelining
triton_kernel[grid](arg_0, arg_1, arg_2, arg_3)
# Results in ~5.5 active warps/scheduler, 86.5% no-eligible cycles
fast_pseudocode:
# Launch with num_warps=8, num_stages=2
triton_kernel[grid](
    arg_0, arg_1, arg_2, arg_3,
    num_warps=8,
    num_stages=2,
)
# Results in ~5.7 active warps/scheduler, 85.9% no-eligible cycles
# Marginal improvement — bank conflicts still dominate
applicable_when: CPIStall rule fires with MIO stall cycles >15 per warp representing >40% of total stall cycles; scheduler No Eligible >80%; active warps per scheduler <8; block_limit_shared_mem > block_limit_registers (shared memory is not the binding occupancy constraint); the MIO stalls are latency-driven (not bank-conflict-driven)
do_not_apply_when: SharedMemoryConflicts rule also fires with >5-way bank conflicts — in that case, bank conflicts are the root cause of MIO stalls and adding more warps only queues more conflicting requests; the block is already limited by shared memory capacity (block_limit_shared_mem is the binding constraint and doubling warps would reduce block count); registers_per_thread is already high and doubling warps would spill to local memory
framework_notes: In Triton, num_warps and num_stages are passed as keyword arguments to the kernel launch: kernel[grid](*args, num_warps=8, num_stages=2). num_warps must be a power of 2. num_stages enables software pipelining of the main loop. In CUDA, the equivalent is choosing a larger block size or using cooperative groups to increase warp-level parallelism per SM.

strategy_title: Preload Small Reused Matrix Into Registers Before K-Loop
strategy_description: When a matrix (e.g., B with shape [K, N]) is small enough to fit entirely in registers and is reused across all K-loop iterations, loading it once before the loop eliminates repeated global memory fetches and shared memory bank conflicts inside the loop. In this case, B (64×4 = 256 floats = 1 KB) was loaded once as a [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] register tile before the k_idx loop, replacing the per-iteration strided global gather that caused 10-way shared memory bank conflicts (80% of shared load wavefronts). The speedup is modest (1.53x) because the dominant bottleneck (SharedMemoryConflicts, CPIStall MIO stalls) persists — the bank conflicts in shared loads were not fully eliminated since the dot product still uses shared memory internally — but the global load traffic inside the loop was removed.
slow_pseudocode:
# B reloaded every k_idx iteration with strided global gather
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A + xindex_a)  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K]
    # Strided B load: B[k, n] at B + (k + 64*n), causes 10-way bank conflicts
    b = tl.load(B + (idx_m + 64 * idx_n))  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
    acc += tl.dot(a, b)
fast_pseudocode:
# Preload entire B once before loop into register tile
b_k_coords = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)[:, None]   # [BLOCK_K, 1]
b_n_coords = offs_b_n[None, :]                  # [1, BLOCK_N]
b_preloaded = tl.load(B + (b_k_coords + 64 * b_n_coords))  # [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N], loaded once

for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A + xindex_a)  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K]
    b = b_preloaded             # reuse register tile, no global load
    acc += tl.dot(a, b)
applicable_when: A matrix operand is small enough to fit in registers (e.g., <4 KB), is reused across all K-loop iterations without change (i.e., the same tile covers the full K dimension), and the per-iteration load causes shared memory bank conflicts or strided global accesses. SharedMemoryConflicts NCU rule fires with high bank conflict way-count (>5x) on shared loads inside the K-loop.
do_not_apply_when: The matrix is too large to fit in registers (causes register spilling and occupancy collapse); the K-loop iterates over different tiles of B (i.e., BLOCK_K < K, so different k_idx values need different B slices — this optimization only works when BLOCK_K == K or there is only one k_idx iteration); register pressure is already high (>64 regs/thread) and adding a register-resident tile would reduce occupancy.
framework_notes: In Triton, loading a 2D tile with tl.load(ptr + (row_idx + stride * col_idx)) where row_idx and col_idx are broadcast index arrays produces a register-resident tensor. This avoids shared memory entirely for the preloaded tile. The optimization is only correct when BLOCK_K equals the full K dimension (single k_idx iteration). For multi-iteration K-loops, a slice selection mechanism (e.g., dynamic_slice) would be needed, which Triton does not support efficiently — in that case, consider shared memory staging with padding instead.

strategy_title: Revert 3D Expand-Sum to tl.dot to Fix Register Spill
strategy_description: When a kernel has been modified to replace tl.dot with a 3D expand-and-sum pattern that causes register spilling (registers/thread at hardware max of 255, theoretical occupancy collapsed to 12.5%, instruction count 3x higher), reverting to tl.dot restores correct register usage (39/thread), occupancy (37.5%), and instruction count (4.7M), cutting duration by ~50%. The only code change needed is replacing the 3D intermediate accumulation with tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=ACC_TYPE); the surrounding load logic and epilogue remain unchanged. This is a corrective revert, not a new optimization — the negative experience (neg_002) documents the anti-pattern and this positive confirms the fix.
slow_pseudocode:
# 3D expand-and-sum: creates [BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_K=64, BLOCK_N=4] intermediate -> spills to local mem
a_3d = tl.expand_dims(a.to(ACC_TYPE), 2)   # [128, 64, 1]
b_3d = tl.expand_dims(b.to(ACC_TYPE), 0)   # [1, 64, 4]
acc = acc + tl.sum(a_3d * b_3d, axis=1)    # [128, 64, 4] -> [128, 4]  SPILLS
fast_pseudocode:
# tl.dot uses shared memory, avoids register spill
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=ACC_TYPE)  # [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]
applicable_when: Kernel shows registers_per_thread at or near hardware maximum (255), theoretical occupancy collapsed to <=12.5%, instruction count 3x+ higher than expected, and UncoalescedSharedAccess/local memory NCU rules firing — all symptoms of a prior 3D expand-and-sum replacement of tl.dot having caused register spill.
do_not_apply_when: The kernel is already using tl.dot correctly (registers/thread ~39, occupancy ~37.5%); or when the 3D intermediate tensor is small enough to fit in registers (BLOCK_M * BLOCK_K * BLOCK_N < ~4K elements).
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False, out_dtype=tl.float32) is the correct way to perform matrix multiplication using shared memory without register spill. The allow_tf32=False flag is critical for FP32 precision. The 3D expand-and-sum anti-pattern (tl.expand_dims + broadcast multiply + tl.sum) materializes a full [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N] tensor that exceeds register file capacity for typical tile sizes.
